correctness.rationale: For each sphere point, the unit constraint gives \(f(0)=1-\|f'\|_\infty\). Substituting \(f'=m_f+\delta_f\) and \(g'=m_g+\delta_g\) cancels both derivative norms and yields the exact kernel \(2+\max_I(\delta_f+\delta_g)\). The converse twin classification is proved by reconstructing every \(\delta(x)\) from \(\inf\{\max_I(\delta+u):0\le u\le1,\ u(x)=1\}=1+\delta(x)\). The fiber interval follows exactly from nonnegativity and the unit constraint, and the fiberwise surjection construction preserves the displayed kernel identically. Endpoint and singleton-fiber cases were checked explicitly.

value.rationale: The result gives the complete kernel of the endpoint positive-sum geometry, not a sampled example or a renamed consequence. It identifies exactly which information norm-additivity loses at \(p=1\), classifies every indistinguishability fiber, and shows that the known affine counterexample is only the largest member of a systematic fiberwise non-rigidity. This directly explains the mechanism behind the endpoint failure and provides a natural quotient object for any future classification of all norm-additive self-maps.
